_about: Who sounds like what. Each friend has a list of voices: the first one that works on the free plan is used. Changing the list remakes that friend's clips.

elevenlabs._voices: Each friend speaks with ONE voice for everything (chat, letters and words), so they always sound like the same person. The first voice in each list is the Egyptian voice made with ElevenLabs Voice Design; the others are fallbacks. Optional chat_voice_ids would give a friend a second voice just for chat (not used: it made them sound like two different people). Toota must only ever get women's or girls' voices.
elevenlabs._model: eleven_turbo_v2_5 costs half the credits of eleven_multilingual_v2 and rambles less with designed voices. Clips made earlier with multilingual v2 are kept.

_pronounce: If a clip sounds wrong (for example a single sound read as a letter name), add the text here with a spelling that reads better, then remake it.

gemini._about: Letter sounds (Toota, slow) are made with Gemini TTS on the free tier (about 10 clips a day; key in the GEMINI_API_KEY secret). Changing the voice or style remakes them. 'overrides' fixes single sounds: a different style and/or text for that sound. Toota's words use 'style_word' (spoken from their vowelled form) and her syllables 'style_syllable'. Clips are made in unit order. (ث uses the plain style: measured, its hiss is soft like ف, a real 'th'; the 'th as in think' instruction made it a loud 's'.) All of Toota's lines use Gemini; chat lines use style_chat. 'first' lists lines to make before anything else (lesson 1's instructions).
gemini.style: Modern Standard Arabic (Fusha), not Egyptian dialect. A warm, gentle female phonics teacher for a 6-year-old says only this one letter sound, clearly and a little slowly: the consonant followed by a short a. Do not say the letter name, and say nothing else.

هَ.style: Modern Standard Arabic (Fusha), not Egyptian dialect. A warm, gentle female phonics teacher for a 6-year-old says only this one letter sound, clearly and a little slowly: the consonant followed by a short a. Do not say the letter name, and say nothing else. Start directly on the soft breathy "h" itself, like the h in English "hat": there must be no vowel or sound at all before the h.

هُ.style: Modern Standard Arabic (Fusha), not Egyptian dialect. A warm, gentle female phonics teacher for a 6-year-old says only this one letter sound, clearly and a little slowly: the consonant followed by a short u (as in "put"). Do not say the letter name, and say nothing else. Start directly on the soft breathy "h" itself, like the h in English "hat": there must be no vowel or sound at all before the h.

هِ.style: Modern Standard Arabic (Fusha), not Egyptian dialect. A warm, gentle female phonics teacher for a 6-year-old says only this one letter sound, clearly and a little slowly: the consonant followed by a short i (as in "sit"). Do not say the letter name, and say nothing else. Start directly on the soft breathy "h" itself, like the h in English "hat": there must be no vowel or sound at all before the h.

gemini.style_word: Modern Standard Arabic (Fusha), not Egyptian dialect. A warm, gentle female teacher for a 6-year-old says this one word clearly and a little slowly, exactly as written with its vowel marks. Start straight on the first letter (no extra sound before it). Say nothing else.
gemini.style_syllable: Modern Standard Arabic (Fusha), not Egyptian dialect. A warm, gentle female phonics teacher for a 6-year-old says this one syllable clearly and slowly, exactly as written with its vowel marks: it is one piece of a word being sounded out. Start straight on the first letter (no extra sound before it). Say nothing else.
gemini.style_chat: Egyptian Arabic (Cairo dialect), read exactly as written. A warm, cheerful, gentle young woman talking to a 6-year-old girl: clear, friendly and a little slow, with a smile in her voice. Say exactly this text and nothing else.
